column10: Are you able to help your friend?

column10: Overall, the conversation was probably a ...
column11: Low-pressure and pleasant chance to meet a new person.
column12: Stressful situation, because the person might have found you uninteresting.

column10: Your friend probably cancelled your plans together because ...
column11: They remembered they had an important meeting at work at the same time.

column10: Do the trembling feelings mean that you are unprepared for the presentation?

column9: In the end, you realize that people were probably just surprised by the sound and turned around reflexively. The shoppers saw that no one was injured and probably felt relieved.
column10: The other shoppers probably felt ...
column11: Relieved that no one was injured.

While deciding whether or not to invite people to your show, you see yourself bombing.
column10: If you invite your friends and family, they will probably think
column11: You looked really silly and hope they're not invited again.
column12: You did a good job and they hope you invite them to future showcases.

column10: Are you able to talk about your divorced parents?

column11: You have the ability to continue with your talk.
column12: You have to stop your talk and flee the situation.

column10: Do you think others will like your presentation?

You have the recipe your parents gave you, but you worry you don't have the cooking skills to pull off the dish. You think that people at the party will probably think your casserole tastes unappetizing.
column10: When you think about the reactions to your casserole, you see the other guests
column11: Leaving their servings on their plates.

Your partner specifically reminded you to pack the sunscreen before leaving the hotel room. Recently, you and your partner have been fighting more than usual, and you think your partner will be angry.
column9: You apologize to your partner, and volunteer to go get sunscreen somewhere. Your partner thanks you for going, and is not upset.
column10: Is your partner mad at you?

column10: Is your coworker judgmental of your bilingual family?

column10: Did your aquaintance get quiet because they were judging you?

column9: You decide to take initiative and ask for their numbers. You feel hopeful
column10: Can you make friends with your colleagues even though everything is online?

column8: You have off on Monday for a holiday, and you know people will make plans for the long weekend. After a close friend said they're out of town for the weekend, you realize you don't have anyone to hang out with for the long weekend. This makes you optimistic about making new friends next week.
column10: Are you sad about the long weekend?

column8: You are at a birthday party for a friend of a friend. You notice that you are flushed and a little sweaty. Standing there, you think that these sensations are normal.
column10: People will probably ...
column11: Not see you sweat since the room is dimly lit.

column8: You see an old friend you haven't spoken to in years. Your heart skips a beat. You feel excited.
column10: Is it OK that your heart felt like it skipped a beat?

column9: After you clean up the mess as best as you can, you realize that their response was a normal, knee-jerk reaction. They say that they are not upset with you, and you believe that they are sincere.
column10: Your coworker is probably ...

column8: There's a personal question that you've been wanting to ask your boss for a while, but you haven't. You picture yourself asking when you meet next. As you think about the question, you feel ready.
column10: Are you looking forward to asking your boss a question?

column8: You walk into a quiet meeting room a few minutes late. The door squeaks really loudly as you enter and your coworkers look in your direction. They are probably feeling surprised.
column10: Are your coworkers annoyed that you disturbed them?

column10: Do you take your acquaintance’s call to meet for coffee?

column10: Did you say the wrong thing?

column10: Do the trembling feelings mean that you are unprepared for the presentation?

column10: Is it too late to befriend your new coworkers?

column10: Do you think your friend's tingly throat is a sign of COVID?

You let them know that you have to be up early tomorrow morning for an important event and that you can't go with them and they seem disappointed. You think that your new friends will respect your decision to put your needs first.
column10: Do your friends judge you for not going out with them?

column9: Afterwards, you realize that many people engage in office gossip from time to time and that your colleagues probably did not mean to make you feel bad. In fact, it is possible that they were saying something positive.
column10: Were your coworkers saying negative things about you?
